newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-EMAP set to continue strong run.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-EMAP set to continue strong run.

text.p: British media company EMAP Plc is expected to report a steep rise in profit on Monday despite a year punctuated by boardroom acrimony and departures.

Analysts estimate pre-tax profit for the year to end March should climb by 40 percent or more to between 110 and 120 million stg from 78.3 million a year ago. Most expect a dividend of around 13 pence per share, up from 11.2 p.
EMAP has reshaped its business in recent years, selling out of its original local newspaper operations and expanding its UK commercial radio and French consumer magazine units.
Newly integrated businesses and a healthy UK advertising market are likely to fuel the profit growth.
But it has not been all plain sailing for EMAP over the past 12 months.
The company was hit by a very public row over corporate governance which resulted in the ousting of two rebel non-executive directors at an extraordinary general meeting in December.

Two months later EMAP announced it was losing long-serving managing director David Arculus to United News & Media. EMAP has opted not to appoint a new managing director to work in tandem with chief executive Robin Miller.
Analysts said that Arculus had been a strong strategist and his departure begged questions about who will provide the vision to take the company forward.

The management issue is complicated by the planned retirement next year of chairman Sir John Hoskyns. Miller has been tipped as a likely successor but his appointment would create a vacancy for a new chief executive.
